title: Keynu Runtime Readiness and Melakat Integration
goal: Harden Keynu into a persistent, resumable software-development and research runtime, then use that runtime to develop, test, and research Melakat without duplicating generic engineering capabilities in the Melakat integration.
currentMilestone: Complete runtime cleanup and establish the Melakat domain integration on the shared Engineering Runtime
completedMilestones: Completed the September 2026 source-driven Keynu runtime audit
Added comprehensive GitHub CI and clean-checkout validation
Implemented restart-safe persistent KAP job claiming and REPORT delivery recovery
Unified post-report continuation for direct and generic runtime jobs
Persisted autonomous continuation counters across restarts
Added cross-platform filesystem containment and protected-memory enforcement
Added the central Engineering Runtime v1 for shared project IO, commands, scripts, Git, and verification
Centralized MissionManager and ContextAssembler active-mission selection through ActiveMissionResolver
nextMilestones: Reconcile workflow continuation with the persistent mission continuation path
Remove only verified generated, backup, and historical runtime garbage without breaking compatibility contracts
Reconcile architecture and status documentation with the current runtime
Add Melakat as a Keynu project and implement a domain-specific MelakatDriver on top of Engineering Runtime
Create resumable Melakat development and research mission templates
Prove an end-to-end restart/resume Melakat mission with verified local actions and experiment evidence
rules: Keynu is a persistent mission runtime, not merely a collection of application drivers.
Continue automatically through safe mission steps after verified reports; ask the human only for real blockers, permissions, destructive actions, or consequential external actions.
Use the central Engineering Runtime for filesystem, shell, PowerShell, Node.js, Git, build, test, and verification work.
Do not duplicate generic software-engineering operations inside MelakatDriver or any future domain driver.
Keep domain repositories as the source of truth for their code, scientific contracts, tests, and evidence artifacts.
Use small independently verifiable KAP jobs and persist reports before relying on them for continuation.
Do not silently replay a side-effecting job after an interrupted or ambiguous execution.
Preserve KAP 1.0 and ADR compatibility surfaces unless an explicit migration is documented and tested.
Run the comprehensive Keynu validation suite before merging runtime changes.
Prefer Node.js and native Node APIs for cross-platform engineering operations; use PowerShell where Windows-specific behavior requires it.
Never overwrite protected Keynu repository memory through generic file operations.
Do not claim an autonomous or scientific result without matching runtime, test, or artifact evidence.

architectureDecisions.title: Engineering Runtime is shared infrastructure
architectureDecisions.summary: All project integrations reuse one project-scoped engineering layer for filesystem, process, script, Git, build, test, and verification operations.

architectureDecisions.title: Domain drivers contain domain semantics only
architectureDecisions.summary: MelakatDriver interprets Melakat experiments and artifacts but delegates ordinary engineering operations to Engineering Runtime.

architectureDecisions.title: Configured mission is authoritative
architectureDecisions.summary: ActiveMissionResolver uses the configured mission as the authority and reconciles stale persisted runtime state before mission bootstrap.

architectureDecisions.title: Persistence precedes autonomous continuation
architectureDecisions.summary: KAP job claims, reports, delivery status, mission state, and continuation counters must be recoverable before Keynu requests the next autonomous AI step.

knownLimitations: A local .keynu mission registry can override repository mission configuration until it is synchronized on the user's machine.
WorkflowContinuationService remains a separate legacy workflow path and is not yet fully reconciled with the persistent browser mission continuation path.
Engineering Runtime v1 is project-scoped and guarded but is not a complete operating-system sandbox.
Repository cleanup candidates still require reference checks before deletion.
MelakatDriver and the end-to-end Melakat mission have not yet been implemented.

nextActions.title: Reconcile workflow and mission continuation
nextActions.reason: Keynu should have one understandable continuation model instead of parallel workflow and browser paths.
